name: Amway Corp.
desc: Direct-selling company that sells nutrition, beauty and home care products through independent distributors in many countries.
markets: Sells through distributor networks in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific (notably China, Korea, Japan) and Latin America.
rationale: Global consumer brand (Nutrilite, Artistry) with large Asian sales; F1 could support brand building and distributor incentive hospitality.

name: Huafon Group
desc: Chinese chemical group making spandex, polyurethane raw materials, adipic acid and other chemical and aluminium materials.
markets: Mainly Chinese textile and chemical customers, with exports of spandex and chemicals to other Asian and overseas markets.
rationale: B2B chemicals maker with little consumer brand; F1 could only serve export customer hospitality, so the fit is weak.

name: Dr. August Oetker KG
desc: Makes Dr. Oetker baking products, frozen pizza and desserts, and owns Radeberger beer and Henkell Freixenet sparkling wine.
markets: Dr. Oetker food sold across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific; Henkell Freixenet sparkling wine exported worldwide.
rationale: Global consumer brands in pizza, beer and sparkling wine could use F1 for product activation and podium-style hospitality.
changed: Family group split between branches in 2021-22; Hamburg Süd shipping sold to Maersk in 2017

name: Mansour Group
desc: Egyptian family conglomerate distributing Caterpillar equipment and General Motors vehicles, plus consumer goods and retail operations.
markets: Egypt is the core market; Caterpillar dealerships (Mantrac) and other businesses operate in further African and other markets.
rationale: Distributes General Motors vehicles in Egypt; GM's Cadillac entered F1 in 2026, giving a possible co-marketing angle in Egypt.

name: VolkerWessels
desc: Dutch construction group building infrastructure, buildings and energy and telecom networks, and developing property.
markets: Operates in the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Germany and North America; no other verified expansion plans.
rationale: Contractor with B2B public-sector clients and limited brand marketing; F1 would serve mainly hospitality, a modest fit.
changed: Listed on Euronext Amsterdam in 2017; taken private again by the Wessels family's Reggeborgh in 2019

name: Barceló Group
desc: Spanish group operating Barceló hotels and resorts and, through Ávoris, travel agencies, tour operators and airlines.
markets: Hotels in Spain, Europe, the Caribbean, Mexico, the United States and the Middle East; travel business mainly Spain.
rationale: Hotel brand in race-hosting regions (Spain, Mexico, Middle East); F1 could drive leisure bookings and guest hospitality.

name: Gilbane, Inc.
desc: Provides construction management and general contracting, and develops and manages real estate, mainly in the United States.
markets: Customers mainly across the United States; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: US-focused contractor with B2B clients; little consumer marketing, so F1 offers only hospitality value.

name: Red Apple Group
desc: Owns United Refining, Kwik Fill and Red Apple fuel stations, Gristedes supermarkets in Manhattan and real estate.
markets: Refining and fuel stations in Pennsylvania, New York and Ohio, supermarkets in New York City; no international activity known.
rationale: Regional US fuel retailer and grocer; fuel retail has some motorsport link, but reach is too local for F1.

name: Tönnies Holding
desc: German meat processor slaughtering pigs and cattle and selling pork, beef and processed meat products.
markets: Processing plants in Germany and other European countries; sells meat across Europe and exports to Asian markets.
rationale: Commodity meat processor selling to retailers; little consumer brand use for F1, so a weak fit.

name: Clark Enterprises, Inc.
desc: Private investment group that owns Clark Construction Group, a US general contractor, plus real estate and other investments.
markets: Clark Construction builds across the United States; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: US building contractor with B2B and government clients; F1 offers little beyond occasional client hospitality.

name: GOLDBECK GmbH
desc: Designs, builds and services commercial buildings such as warehouses, offices, schools and multi-storey car parks.
markets: Mainly Germany, with branches in other European countries such as Austria, Switzerland, Poland, Czechia and the UK.
rationale: European B2B builder; F1 offers only client hospitality and limited brand value, so a modest fit.

name: Lars Larsen Group A/S
desc: Danish family holding company that owns the JYSK home furnishing chain and other furniture and bedding retailers.
markets: JYSK stores mainly across Europe, plus Canada and franchised stores in other regions; furniture chains mainly in Scandinavia.
rationale: Large European home retailer with mass-market advertising; F1 could support JYSK brand across Europe, but fit is not obvious.

name: Breakthru Beverage Group
desc: Wholesale distributor of wine, spirits and beer to retailers, bars and restaurants in the United States and Canada.
markets: Distribution in many US states and in Canada; no verified operations outside North America.
rationale: Distributor rather than brand owner; F1 links run through the drinks brands it carries, so direct fit is weak.
changed: Formed in 2016 from the merger of Wirtz Beverage Group and Charmer Sunbelt Group

name: Diersch & Schröder Group
desc: German group trading mineral oil products, fuels and chemicals, and operating tank storage and lubricant businesses.
markets: Trading customers in Germany and Europe with some wider international trading; extent not verified.
rationale: Low-profile B2B fuel and chemicals trader; little use for F1 brand exposure, a weak fit.

name: Uline, Inc.
desc: Distributes shipping, packaging, janitorial and industrial supplies to businesses by catalogue and online.
markets: Customers in the United States, Canada and Mexico; no verified expansion beyond North America.
rationale: North American B2B supplier relying on catalogues; F1's global audience offers limited value, though US races exist.

name: VDL Groep B.V.
desc: Dutch industrial group making buses and coaches, contract-built cars, semiconductor equipment parts and other industrial products.
markets: Companies across Europe, with operations in North America and Asia; supplies customers such as ASML; buses sold in Europe.
rationale: Engineering group with automotive history; F1 could showcase manufacturing technology to B2B clients, but fit is plausible not obvious.

name: Hilti AG
desc: Makes and sells power tools, anchors, fastening systems and software for professional construction customers worldwide.
markets: Direct sales organisations in over 100 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Global premium B2B tool brand; rival tool brands (DeWalt, Einhell) sponsor F1, supporting a technology and hospitality case.

name: Wieland-Werke AG
desc: Makes semi-finished copper and copper alloy products such as strip, tubes, rods and wire for industry.
markets: Plants and sales in Europe, North America and Asia; serves automotive, electrical and building industries.
rationale: B2B metals supplier with automotive customers; F1 could support hospitality, but brand value is limited.
changed: Acquired Global Brass and Copper (US) in 2019

name: J.D. Heiskell Holdings
desc: US agribusiness merchandising grain and animal feed ingredients, mainly for dairy and livestock producers.
markets: Customers mainly US dairy and livestock producers; no verified international operations.
rationale: Commodity feed trader serving farmers; no consumer brand and little reason to use F1.

name: Demoulas Super Markets, Inc.
desc: Operates the Market Basket supermarket chain in Massachusetts, New Hampshire and Maine.
markets: Customers in New England only; no verified expansion plans outside the region.
rationale: Regional US grocer with low-price model and little advertising; F1 makes little sense.

name: XXXLutz Group
desc: Austrian furniture retailer running XXXLutz, Möbelix, Mömax and other furniture stores and online shops.
markets: Stores in Austria, Germany, Switzerland, Sweden and several Central and Eastern European countries.
rationale: Heavy advertiser in German-speaking Europe; F1 could reach its core markets, but furniture retail is not an obvious fit.

name: CLAAS KGaA mbH
desc: Makes combine harvesters, forage harvesters, tractors and other agricultural machinery for farmers worldwide.
markets: Factories in Europe, the US, India and China; sells through dealers across Europe, the Americas and Asia.
rationale: Machinery brand with engineering image; F1 could support dealer hospitality, but its farmer audience overlaps weakly.

name: New Balance Athletics, Inc.
desc: Designs, makes and sells athletic shoes, sportswear and lifestyle footwear sold worldwide.
markets: Sells across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions through retail, wholesale and online channels.
rationale: Global sportswear brand; rivals adidas and Puma are F1 partners, making team kit or lifestyle collaborations an obvious route.

name: Harbor Freight Tools
desc: Discount retailer selling hand tools, power tools, automotive and garden equipment through stores and online.
markets: Stores across the United States only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: US-only tool retailer with automotive DIY customers; US races give some value, but no international reach.

name: Trammo, Inc.
desc: Trades, ships and distributes ammonia, fertilizers, sulphur, petroleum coke and other industrial commodities worldwide.
markets: Trading operations and customers across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia.
rationale: Low-profile commodity trader with few end customers; F1 offers little marketing value.

name: Borusan Holding
desc: Turkish group in steel pipes, Caterpillar equipment distribution, BMW car distribution, logistics and renewable energy.
markets: Mainly Türkiye, with pipe plants in the US and machinery dealerships in Central Asia and the Caucasus.
rationale: Distributes BMW in Türkiye and has motorsport ties at home; F1 hospitality could serve Turkish B2B and premium customers.

name: Chick-fil-A (CFA Properties, Inc.)
desc: Fast-food chain serving chicken sandwiches and meals through franchised and company restaurants.
markets: Restaurants mainly in the US, plus Canada and Puerto Rico; has opened or announced restaurants in the UK and Asia.
rationale: Big US consumer brand with sports marketing (college football); F1 US races could help, but core business is domestic.

name: Zorlu Holding
desc: Turkish conglomerate owning Vestel consumer electronics and appliances, Zorlu Energy, textiles and property businesses.
markets: Vestel exports TVs and appliances widely across Europe; energy and textile operations in Türkiye and abroad.
rationale: Vestel's European consumer electronics sales could use F1 for brand building, though it sells many products under other labels.

name: DRÄXLMAIER Group
desc: Automotive supplier making wiring harnesses, interiors, electrical and battery systems for premium carmakers.
markets: Plants across Europe, North Africa, the Americas and Asia, supplying premium carmakers globally.
rationale: Premium automotive supplier; F1 could showcase electrification know-how to OEM clients, but it has no consumer brand.

name: AMAG Group AG
desc: Swiss importer, dealer and leasing provider for Volkswagen Group cars, including VW, Audi, SEAT, Cupra, Škoda and Porsche.
markets: Customers in Switzerland only; no verified operations abroad.
rationale: Imports Audi into Switzerland; Audi's F1 works team from 2026 offers a local co-marketing angle, but reach is domestic.

name: Raley's Inc.
desc: Operates Raley's, Bel Air, Nob Hill Foods and other supermarkets in Northern California and Nevada.
markets: Customers in Northern California and Nevada only; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Regional US grocer with local marketing and no international customers; F1 makes little commercial sense.

name: Arnold Clark Automobiles Ltd.
desc: Sells new and used cars through franchised dealerships and provides car rental, servicing and finance in the UK.
markets: Dealerships and rental branches in Scotland, England and Wales; no verified operations abroad.
rationale: UK car retailer with strong advertising; British GP audience overlaps, but reach is purely domestic.

name: Bestway Group
desc: Runs Bestway and Batleys cash-and-carry wholesale and Well Pharmacy in the UK, and cement manufacturing in Pakistan.
markets: Wholesale and pharmacy customers in the UK; cement production and banking interests in Pakistan.
rationale: Wholesale and pharmacy businesses aim at UK retailers and patients; F1 offers little, a weak fit.

name: Asklepios Kliniken
desc: Operates hospitals, specialist clinics, rehabilitation centres and care facilities, mainly in Germany.
markets: Patients mainly in Germany; Rhön-Klinikum is majority-owned; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic hospital operator funded largely by public insurance; F1 sponsorship makes little sense.
changed: Took majority control of listed hospital group Rhön-Klinikum in 2020

name: Cremonini S.p.A.
desc: Italian food group in beef processing (Inalca), foodservice distribution (MARR) and travel catering (Chef Express).
markets: Mainly Italy, with Inalca meat exports and operations in Europe, Africa and other markets.
rationale: Mostly B2B food businesses with modest consumer branding; Italian GP hospitality possible but fit is weak.

name: The Walsh Group
desc: General contractor building transportation infrastructure, water projects and commercial and public buildings in North America.
markets: Projects across the United States and in Canada; no verified operations elsewhere.
rationale: B2B contractor with public-sector clients; F1 offers only hospitality, little brand value.

name: Voith GmbH & Co. KGaA
desc: Makes paper machines, hydropower turbines and generators, and drive and transmission systems for industry and transport.
markets: Operations and customers in Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific, including China, India and Brazil.
rationale: Engineering brand serving industrial clients worldwide; F1 could provide technology showcase and hospitality, a plausible fit.

name: Xignux S.A. de C.V.
desc: Mexican industrial group making electrical cables and power equipment, with a packaged food business.
markets: Mainly Mexico and the United States, with other operations in Latin America.
rationale: Mexican B2B industrial group; Mexico City GP hospitality could serve utility clients, but brand use is limited.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to sell its 50% stake in transformer maker Prolec GE to GE Vernova

name: Rich Products Corporation
desc: Makes frozen foods, non-dairy toppings, icings, bakery products and pizza for foodservice, in-store bakeries and retailers.
markets: Sells in over 100 countries, with operations in North America, Latin America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Mostly B2B foodservice supplier with weak consumer branding; F1 offers limited value.

name: AmTrust Financial Services, Inc.
desc: Provides property and casualty insurance, mainly workers' compensation and commercial cover for small businesses, plus warranty products.
markets: Mainly United States, with insurance operations in the UK and continental Europe.
rationale: Insurer selling via brokers to small businesses; F1 could support broker hospitality, but fit is weak.
changed: Taken private in 2018 by its founding families with Stone Point Capital

name: Groupe Pomona
desc: French foodservice wholesaler supplying fruit, vegetables, seafood, dairy and grocery products to restaurants, caterers and shops.
markets: Customers in France; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic B2B food distributor serving French restaurants; no meaningful use for global F1 exposure.

name: Grupo Lala S.A.B. de C.V.
desc: Mexican dairy company making and selling milk, yoghurt, cheese and other dairy products under Lala and other brands.
markets: Mainly Mexico, with operations in the United States and Central America; current Brazil activity not verified.
rationale: Major Mexican consumer brand; Mexico City GP and Latin American F1 fandom give a plausible marketing case.
changed: Delisted from the Mexican Stock Exchange in 2022 after a tender offer by its controlling families

name: Andreas Stihl AG & Co. KG
desc: Makes chainsaws, trimmers, leaf blowers and other petrol and battery-powered outdoor power tools sold through dealers.
markets: Sells in over 160 countries, with factories in Germany, the US, China, Brazil and other countries.
rationale: Strong global consumer and professional brand; tool rivals sponsor F1, giving a plausible brand and dealer hospitality case.

name: Miele & Cie. KG
desc: Makes premium washing machines, dishwashers, vacuum cleaners, kitchen appliances and commercial cleaning equipment.
markets: Sells across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and other regions; growing in China and the US.
rationale: Premium German consumer brand seeking growth in US and Asian markets; F1 suits its quality and engineering image.

name: TRUMPF SE + Co. KG
desc: Makes machine tools for sheet-metal processing, industrial lasers and EUV laser systems for chipmaking equipment.
markets: Subsidiaries and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia, including China and Japan.
rationale: High-tech B2B manufacturer; F1 could showcase precision and laser technology to industrial clients.

name: D&H Distributing Co.
desc: Distributes IT, consumer electronics and technology products to resellers and retailers in the United States and Canada.
markets: Reseller customers in the United States and Canada; no verified operations elsewhere.
rationale: B2B IT distributor; tech vendors it carries sponsor F1, but its own brand reach is limited.

name: Consolidated Electrical Distributors, Inc.
desc: Distributes electrical supplies and equipment to contractors and industry through many branches across the United States.
markets: Branches across the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: Low-profile domestic B2B electrical distributor with no consumer brand; F1 offers little value.

name: Roquette Frères S.A.
desc: Makes starches, polyols, plant proteins and excipients for food, pharmaceutical, nutrition and industrial customers.
markets: Plants and customers in Europe, the Americas and Asia, serving food and pharmaceutical makers worldwide.
rationale: B2B ingredients maker with no consumer brand; F1 makes little sense beyond hospitality.
changed: Acquired IFF's Pharma Solutions business in 2025

name: MANN + HUMMEL International GmbH & Co. KG
desc: Makes air, oil, fuel and cabin filters for vehicles, plus industrial and building air and water filtration.
markets: Plants and sales across Europe, the Americas and Asia; MANN-FILTER sold to workshops worldwide.
rationale: Automotive aftermarket brand (MANN-FILTER) with motorsport-friendly customers; F1 could support workshop and OEM marketing.

name: Asplundh Tree Expert Co.
desc: Provides tree trimming, vegetation management and utility line services for electric utilities and municipalities.
markets: Customers in the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.
rationale: Service contractor for utilities; no consumer brand and little use for F1.

name: Panda Restaurant Group
desc: Operates the Panda Express fast-casual Chinese restaurant chain, plus Panda Inn and other restaurant brands.
markets: Mostly United States restaurants, with smaller numbers in Canada, Mexico, the Middle East and Asia.
rationale: US consumer brand with limited international footprint; F1 US races could help, but fit is not obvious.

name: Kraft Group
desc: Owns the New England Patriots, New England Revolution and Gillette Stadium, plus packaging and paper businesses.
markets: Sports and venue operations in New England; paper and packaging businesses mainly in the United States.
rationale: Sports owner with venue and hospitality expertise; possible interest in F1 hospitality or partnerships, but no clear marketing need.

name: Westcoast Group Holdings Ltd.
desc: Distributes IT products, consumer electronics and office technology to resellers and retailers.
markets: Customers mainly in the UK and Ireland; other European activity not verified.
rationale: B2B tech distributor; British GP hospitality for reseller partners is possible, but brand value is limited.

name: Grimaldi Group S.p.A.
desc: Shipping group operating ro-ro car carriers, ferries and cargo services, including Finnlines and Minoan Lines.
markets: Routes across the Mediterranean, Northern Europe, West Africa and the Americas.
rationale: Major carmaker logistics carrier and ferry brand; F1 hospitality could serve automotive clients, a plausible fit.

name: Bestseller A/S
desc: Danish fashion company designing and selling clothing brands such as Jack & Jones, Vero Moda, Only and Selected.
markets: Sells across Europe, China, India, the Middle East, Canada and other markets through stores and online.
rationale: Global fashion group with young audiences; fashion brands (Tommy Hilfiger, Pepe Jeans) are F1 partners, a good fit.

name: Ben E. Keith Company
desc: Distributes food to restaurants and institutions and Anheuser-Busch beers to retailers in Texas and southern states.
markets: Customers in Texas and other southern and central US states; no international operations known.
rationale: Regional US distributor; F1 offers little, though the Austin GP is in its home market.

name: ALPLA Group
desc: Makes plastic bottles, closures and packaging and recycles PET for consumer goods companies.
markets: Plants in about 45 countries across Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia; serves global consumer-goods brands.
rationale: B2B packaging maker serving brands that sponsor F1; little own brand marketing, so a weak fit.

name: REHAU Group
desc: Makes polymer-based products such as window profiles, pipes, heating and furniture components for building and industry.
markets: Operations and sales across Europe, the Americas and Asia; no verified changes in markets.
rationale: B2B polymer maker with modest consumer branding; F1 could only serve client hospitality, a weak fit.

name: European Metal Recycling Ltd.
desc: Collects, processes and sells scrap metal and recovered materials from vehicles, industry and consumers.
markets: Recycling sites in the UK, the United States and the Netherlands; sells metals to mills worldwide.
rationale: Recycling business with sustainability story but little consumer brand; F1 fit is weak.

name: Grupo Antolín
desc: Makes car interior components such as headliners, door panels, lighting and cockpits for carmakers.
markets: Plants in Europe, the Americas, Asia and Africa, supplying carmakers worldwide.
rationale: Tier-one automotive supplier; F1 could support OEM relationships and technology image, but it lacks a consumer brand.

name: Estes Express Lines, Inc.
desc: Less-than-truckload freight carrier moving business shipments through a terminal network across the United States.
markets: Customers across the United States, with cross-border service to Canada and Mexico through partners.
rationale: US trucking company with B2B shippers; F1 offers little beyond US race hospitality.

name: Grundfos Group
desc: Makes pumps and water solutions for buildings, heating and cooling, water utilities and industry.
markets: Sales companies and factories across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific, including China and India.
rationale: Global engineering brand with sustainability and efficiency messaging; F1 could provide B2B hospitality and technology storytelling.

name: Webasto Group
desc: Automotive supplier making sunroofs, convertible roofs, vehicle heaters, battery systems and EV charging products.
markets: Plants and sales across Europe, the Americas and Asia, supplying carmakers and aftermarket customers.
rationale: Automotive supplier with an aftermarket brand; F1 could support OEM relations, but marketing value is moderate.

name: GALLO (E&J Gallo Winery)
desc: Makes, imports and markets wines and spirits under brands such as Barefoot, Apothic and New Amsterdam.
markets: Mainly United States, with exports to many countries in Europe, Asia and other regions.
rationale: Large drinks marketer; spirits and wine brands use F1 (Moët, Chivas, Jack Daniel's), so a brand-led case exists.

name: Oldendorff Carriers GmbH & Co. KG
desc: Dry bulk shipping company carrying coal, iron ore, grain and other bulk cargoes with owned and chartered ships.
markets: Customers and offices worldwide, including Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: B2B dry bulk shipping firm without a consumer brand; F1 offers little marketing value.

name: Musgrave Group
desc: Food wholesaler and franchisor supplying SuperValu, Centra, Daybreak and other independent retailers and foodservice customers.
markets: Customers in the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland; no verified further expansion plans.
rationale: Irish grocery brands with domestic focus; F1 offers limited value for their markets.

name: SEW-EURODRIVE Group
desc: Makes electric motors, gear units, frequency inverters and drive automation systems for industrial machinery.
markets: Plants and assembly centres across Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B drive maker; F1 could serve engineering hospitality, but little brand need.

name: Galeries Lafayette Group
desc: Runs Galeries Lafayette department stores and other retail and commerce businesses, mainly in France.
markets: Mainly France, with Galeries Lafayette stores abroad in markets such as the Middle East and China, partly via partners.
rationale: Luxury and fashion retailer with tourist customers; F1 could support premium brand events, but fit is not obvious.
changed: Agreed in 2023 to sell the BHV Marais department store to SGM

name: M.A. Mortenson Companies, Inc.
desc: Builds sports and entertainment venues, healthcare, commercial and data-centre buildings, and wind and solar projects.
markets: Projects mainly in the United States, with some work in Canada; no verified wider international plans.
rationale: Builder of stadiums and data centres with B2B clients; F1 has little marketing value for it.

name: Laing O’Rourke Corporation
desc: Engineering and construction contractor delivering infrastructure, buildings and energy projects using off-site manufacturing.
markets: Projects in the United Kingdom and Australia; no verified expansion into other regions.
rationale: B2B contractor with public and corporate clients; F1 offers limited brand value beyond hospitality.

name: Müller Holding Ltd. & Co. KG
desc: Operates the Müller drugstore chain selling cosmetics, toiletries, perfume, toys, stationery and household goods.
markets: Stores in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Spain, Croatia, Slovenia and Hungary.
rationale: European consumer retailer with mass audience; F1 reaches its markets, but retail chains rarely gain much.

name: Messer Group
desc: Produces and supplies industrial, medical and specialty gases and gas application technology.
markets: Operations in Europe, the Americas and Asia, including China and Vietnam.
rationale: B2B gases supplier; little brand use for F1, though it could serve client hospitality.
changed: Bought CVC's stake in Messer Americas in 2023

name: Menarini Group
desc: Italian pharmaceutical company developing, making and selling prescription medicines, consumer health products and diagnostics.
markets: Sells in over 140 countries; strong in Europe, Central Asia, Asia-Pacific, the US (Stemline) and Latin America.
rationale: Pharma marketing is restricted, but consumer health brands and Italian identity give a modest case.

name: Chimet S.p.A.
desc: Italian company recovering and refining gold, silver, platinum and palladium from scrap, catalysts and industrial waste.
markets: Mainly Italian jewellery and industrial customers; international reach not verified.
rationale: B2B precious metals refiner with no consumer brand; F1 makes little sense.

name: Rigby Group
desc: UK family group owning IT services company SCC, regional airports, aviation services and hotels.
markets: Mainly UK, with SCC operations in France and other European countries.
rationale: SCC's enterprise IT clients could be hosted at F1, and its tech partners sponsor F1; a plausible fit.

name: Intersnack Group
desc: Makes crisps, nuts and savoury snacks under brands such as funny-frisch, Chio, KP, Tyrrells and Pom-Bär.
markets: Sells mainly across Europe, including Germany, the UK, France and Central and Eastern Europe.
rationale: Consumer snack brands with mass audiences; F1 suits product activation in Europe, plausible but not obvious.

name: Omya AG
desc: Produces calcium carbonate and other industrial minerals and distributes specialty chemicals to industry.
markets: Plants and customers in over 50 countries across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B minerals producer with no consumer brand or end-customer marketing; F1 makes little sense.

name: Festo SE & Co. KG
desc: Makes pneumatic and electric automation components and systems, and provides technical training for industry.
markets: Sales companies in about 60 countries across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Automation brand with innovation image; F1 could showcase engineering to industrial clients, plausible fit.

name: MAPEI S.p.A.
desc: Makes adhesives, sealants, mortars and chemical products for building, flooring and infrastructure.
markets: Plants and subsidiaries across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, Africa and the Middle East.
rationale: Brand with strong sports sponsorship history (football, cycling); F1 could extend global brand building and B2B hospitality.

name: TJ Morris Ltd. (Home Bargains)
desc: Operates Home Bargains and Quality Save discount stores selling groceries, household goods and toiletries.
markets: Stores across the United Kingdom only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Domestic UK discount retailer with low marketing spend and no overseas stores; F1 makes little sense.

name: Aars AS
desc: Norwegian family-owned company that the ranking links to Møller Mobility Group, a Volkswagen Group car importer and dealer.
markets: Møller Mobility Group operates in Norway, Sweden and the Baltic states; ownership link not verified.
rationale: Importer of Audi and other VW brands; Audi's F1 team could support local promotion, but reach is regional.

name: Veronesi Holding
desc: Italian group making animal feed, poultry and turkey products (AIA) and cured meats (Negroni).
markets: Mainly Italian customers, with some exports; no verified international operations.
rationale: Strong Italian consumer brands; Italian GP activation is possible, but reach is mainly domestic.

name: FRITZ EGGER GmbH & Co. OG
desc: Makes wood-based panels, laminate flooring, decorative surfaces and timber products for furniture and building.
markets: Plants in Europe, Russia, Türkiye, Argentina and the United States; sells across Europe and the Americas.
rationale: Sponsors alpine skiing; F1 could support B2B dealer hospitality, but fit is modest.

name: PHW Group (Lohmann & Co. AG)
desc: German poultry producer making chicken and turkey products under the Wiesenhof brand, plus feed and animal health products.
markets: Mainly German retail customers, with some operations and sales elsewhere in Europe.
rationale: Domestic food brand with football sponsorship history; F1 offers limited extra value.

name: CRONIMET Holding Group
desc: Trades and recycles stainless steel scrap, ferroalloys and other metals for steel mills and foundries.
markets: Operations in Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia; supplies steel producers worldwide.
rationale: B2B metals trader and recycler without a consumer brand; F1 makes little commercial sense.

name: VKR Group
desc: Danish holding owning Velux roof windows and skylights and other building, daylight and ventilation businesses.
markets: Velux sells across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and other regions with factories in many countries.
rationale: Global consumer-facing building brand with sustainability messaging; F1 could raise awareness, plausible fit.

name: Diehl Stiftung & Co. KG
desc: German group making defence systems, metal semi-finished products, controls, metering devices and aircraft cabin equipment.
markets: Operations in Europe, North America and Asia, serving defence, automotive, utility and aviation customers.
rationale: Diversified engineering group, but defence makes it sensitive; civil divisions offer only weak F1 value.

name: Viessmann Group
desc: Family holding making commercial refrigeration systems after selling its heating and climate business to Carrier.
markets: Refrigeration customers mainly in Europe; heating business now belongs to Carrier.
rationale: Remaining business is B2B commercial refrigeration with little brand need; F1 offers little value.
changed: Sold heating business Viessmann Climate Solutions to Carrier Global in 2024

name: Merkur Group
desc: German gaming group making gaming machines and operating amusement arcades, casinos and sports betting.
markets: Mainly Germany, with operations in the UK, Spain and other European countries.
rationale: Gaming brands sponsor F1 (Play'n GO, Betway), but gambling advertising rules limit use.

name: Stena Metall AB
desc: Swedish group recycling metals and other materials and trading steel, aluminium and oil products.
markets: Operations mainly in Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland and Poland.
rationale: Nordic B2B recycler and steel trader without a consumer brand; F1 makes little sense.

name: Agrosuper S.A.
desc: Chilean food company producing and selling pork, chicken, turkey and farmed salmon under Super Pollo and other brands.
markets: Strong in Chile, with exports to Asia, the United States, Latin America and Europe.
rationale: Leading Chilean consumer food brand; exports are B2B commodities, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Vaillant Group
desc: Makes gas boilers, heat pumps, water heaters and home energy systems under Vaillant, Saunier Duval and other brands.
markets: Sells mainly across Europe, with operations in China, Türkiye and other markets.
rationale: European heating brand promoting heat pumps; F1 could support installer hospitality, but fit is modest.

name: Bet365 Group Ltd.
desc: Online gambling company offering sports betting, casino, poker and games to customers through its website and apps.
markets: Customers in the UK, Europe, Canada, many US states, Australia and Latin America.
rationale: Betting brands (Betway, FanDuel) are F1 partners; bet365's sports audience fits well where gambling sponsorship is allowed.

name: MD S.p.A.
desc: Operates MD discount supermarkets selling groceries and household products across Italy.
markets: Stores across Italy only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic Italian discount grocer with price-led marketing; little use for global F1 exposure.

name: Endress+Hauser AG
desc: Makes measurement instruments, sensors and automation solutions for process industries such as chemicals, food and water.
markets: Sales centres and plants across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B instrument maker; F1 could serve data and precision storytelling with clients, a plausible but niche fit.

name: Delaware North Companies, Inc.
desc: Provides food, beverage, retail and hospitality services at stadiums, airports, parks, resorts and casinos.
markets: Mainly United States, with operations in the UK, Australia and New Zealand.
rationale: Owns the Boston Bruins and runs sports venue hospitality; F1 events could be a hospitality business opportunity.

name: H.T. Hackney Company
desc: Wholesale distributor supplying groceries, tobacco and other goods to convenience stores and independent retailers.
markets: Retail customers in eastern and southern US states; no international operations known.
rationale: Regional US wholesaler with no consumer brand and no international customers; F1 makes little sense.

name: Samuel, Son & Co. Ltd.
desc: Processes and distributes steel, aluminium and other metals and makes industrial packaging and products.
markets: Customers mainly in Canada and the United States; no verified wider international operations.
rationale: B2B metals distributor; F1 has little marketing value for it, though the Canadian GP is local.

name: Cevital Group
desc: Algerian conglomerate producing sugar and edible oils, and active in retail, electronics, appliances, steel and industry.
markets: Mainly Algeria, with exports and owned businesses in France and other European countries.
rationale: Large North African consumer brand; F1 reach in Algeria is limited, so a weak fit.

name: Hellmann Worldwide Logistics
desc: Provides air, sea and road freight forwarding, contract logistics and courier services for businesses worldwide.
markets: Offices and partner networks across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Logistics brand could use F1 for B2B hospitality; rivals DHL and CEVA are F1 partners.
